content:
Federal cargo truckers staged a peaceful mobilization across Tamaulipas on Monday morning, October 26, including at the access to Nuevo Laredo, where units were placed on the road's lateral lanes without blocking traffic, according to the Tamaulipas state spokesperson's office (Vocería) and Noticias del Altiplano Tamaulipas.

The action began at 8:00 a.m. and covered three points in the state. At the Nuevo Laredo access, trucks lined the laterals and the roadway itself stayed open. On the Reynosa–Río Bravo highway, trucks circulated at low speed with one lane left open for traffic. The same slow-circulation format applied on the Tampico–El Mante stretch near Altamira, where one lane also remained available.

State and municipal authorities said they were providing the services needed so private vehicles and public transport could keep circulating normally, and that they would report developments as the day went on. Drivers were advised to plan their trips ahead, allow extra travel time, drive with caution and watch official notices.

The Tamaulipas action is part of a wider national truckers mobilization reported across Mexico on Monday. For cross-border travelers, the related national list also flagged the Carretera a Laredo in Nuevo León, at kilometer 14, where trucks were placed on a lateral lane in the south-to-north direction.

title: Truckers mobilize at Nuevo Laredo access and two other Tamaulipas highways — no blockades, officials say
